record.original_question: For H(n) defined from the divisor sequence of n by summing 1 / (d_j - d_i) over all pairs of distinct divisors d_i < d_j, are there only finitely many exceptions to the inequality H(n) < tau(n)?

evidence.quote: the question are there finitely many exceptions to the inequality H(n) < tau (n) remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $1 = d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_{\tau(n)} = n$ be the increasing sequence of positive divisors of $n$, where $\tau(n)$ denotes the number of divisors of $n$. Define
$$H(n) = \sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i}.$$
Determine whether there are only finitely many positive integers $n$ for which the inequality $H(n) < \tau(n)$ fails to hold; equivalently, prove or disprove that $H(n) < \tau(n)$ holds for all but finitely many $n$.
